sentinel_issue: The observed room count reached 50,657 on September 3–10 and remains 46,522 on September 11–12, about 9–10 times the documented 5,120-room cap. This indicates the configured room quota is not enforced as specified, weakening the claimed bound on namespace and disk exposure.
worker_response: The data shows the documented 5,120 cap was not the active global cap: rooms_capacity was exactly 81,920 (16×5,120) on September 3–10 and 163,840 (32×5,120) on September 11–12, matching a multiplied namespace/worker configuration rather than random overflow; room totals stayed below those effective limits and reaping reduced 50,657 to 46,522. Fix by enforcing 5,120 with one shared atomic global counter (or explicitly document per-namespace caps), and expose the effective cap so telemetry cannot imply a single 5,120-room bound when deployment-wide capacity is 16–32 times larger.
auditor_verdict: AGREE, with qualification: rooms_capacity is exactly 81,920 (16×5,120) on September 3–10 and 163,840 (32×5,120) on September 11–12, while totals of 50,657 and 46,522 remain below those telemetry limits and reaping reduced the count by 4,135. The data supports a larger effective configured capacity, but alone cannot prove whether it is a global or per-namespace enforced cap; exposing and enforcing a shared 5,120 counter, or documenting the multiplied limits, is warranted.
